items.note: Notes that Bhoja's parentage, succession, date of succession and death still bristle with controversies.
Names the Samarangana Sutradhara among Bhoja's own works that throw light on Indian life and thought.
Paramaras became the most powerful rulers of northern and central India for a time, rising under Vakpati Munja and reaching their zenith under Bhoja.
The Udaipur-prasasti is the only document giving an apparently complete list of the earlier Paramara rulers; other lists are imperfect.
Siyaka-Sriharsa was Bhoja's grandfather per the plates.
In the list drawn from the Malwa inscriptions, Krsnarajadeva stands as the first historical ruler of the Paramara dynasty.
The Udaipur-Prasasti alone presents an unbroken line of kings from Upendra to Udayaditya.
Origin legend: Vasistha created a hero from the fire-pit who retrieved the cow and was named Paramara.
In the Udaipur-Prasasti Upendra is the first historical king of the dynasty.
The Harsola plates, earliest Paramara records yet found, name Bappairaja first in the genealogy.
Udaipur-prasasti tells that from Vairisimha sprang Siyaka, and from him Vakpati.
Vaidya notes that the Udaipur-prasasti alone names Upendra as first king and puts three kings before Vairisimha II, which he calls reduplication of names.
Vaidya holds the official land-grants should be followed instead of the Udaipur-prasasti of much later date.

items.note: Genealogical table makes Upendra alias Krsnaraja the first historical Paramara and Bhoja the 9th king.

The descriptions of Vairisimha I, Siyaka I and Vakpati I seem purely conventional; only the Udaipur-prasasti mentions all three names.
Concludes Upendra's reign began sometime between A.D. 800 and 840.
Udaipur-prasasti gives Sindhuraja only verse 16, with the single fact that he conquered a king of the Hunas.

Concludes Munja was succeeded by Sindhuraja and Bhoja ascended the throne after Sindhuraja.
